findings.F1: The tested relation points the way the idea predicts but is far too small to clear the bar or a trade's cost: step 5's pooled slope t is 1.70 on 4,236 non-overlapping cases. Per case the unusual move is +0.10 % over 48 hours, a strength of 0.016, about a third of the usual 0.05 (findings F10). That is 0.5 times the 0.19 % cost of a buy and a sell (findings F11).
findings.F2: The effect is mixed across coins and drowned by the market's own moves.
findings.F3: The gain sits in the deepest falls only.
findings.F4: The 48-hour horizon is not where the relation is clearest.
findings.F5: The 20:00 UTC hour is not where the rebound shows; it is among the weakest hours.
findings.F6: The rebound follows falls made as a grind, the opposite of the brief's jump story.
findings.F7: The rebound shows mainly while the coin is below its level of 30 days earlier: slope t 1.90 (2,768 cases) there, against -0.53 (1,496 cases) after a 30-day rise.
findings.F8: Without the clip to falls, the evening's raw 24-hour return has no linear relation to the next 48 hours (slope t -0.65, 8,446 cases). The relation is U-shaped: both extreme quintiles are followed by about +0.3 % (falls of -6.2 %: +0.30 %; rises of +6.5 %: +0.27 %), and the middle three by -0.20 % to -0.36 %.

ideas.name: evening fall rebound, more coins
ideas.idea: The more a coin has fallen over the 24 hours up to the 20:00 UTC close, the more it rises over the next 2 days.
ideas.consequence: An evening long after a deep daily fall is paid by holding it for a day or two, where the rebound is larger than a round trip, not by selling two hours later.

ideas.idea: The more a coin has fallen over the 24 hours up to the 20:00 UTC close, the more it rises over the next 2 days, only while that fall was made of many small hourly steps rather than a few large hours.
ideas.consequence: An evening long after a deep fall is worth holding for two days when the fall was a grind, and not when one or two violent hours made it.
ideas.name: evening grind-fall rebound
